title: Gate manifest
description: The single source of truth for bootstrap-v2 skill-to-CI sync (ADR-0041). A consumer repo commits a gate-manifest.json conforming to this schema; the parity gate, the manifest-driven aggregator, and esk-init genesis all read it.

version.description: The skills version this repo is pinned to (semver). A repo resolves exactly one effective version from this field.

generatedFrom.description: Optional provenance: the upstream repo@version this manifest was generated from.

gates.description: Every gate that must exist in the consumer repo. The manifest is an allow-list: a committed gate script not listed here is unsanctioned and must be rejected.

machinery.description: Non-gate scripts that genesis also installs and that must stay intact (the aggregator that runs the gates). They are not gates (they do not judge code), but a neutered one would turn enforcement off, so they are hash-checked the same way gates are: the upstream-integrity gate at the source, and the parity and provenance gates in a consumer. Optional.

aggregator.description: The single branch-protection status check all gates feed, so adding/removing a gate never changes the required-check set.

requiredCheck.description: The exact status-check context name required in branch protection (e.g. the ruleset's required check).

id.description: Identifier for the gate (kebab-case). Must be unique across gates and map to exactly one script; that uniqueness is enforced by the parity gate, not by this schema (JSON Schema cannot express per-property cross-item uniqueness).

origin.description: upstream = governed by the published skills release (whole-manifest provenance hash-compares these); repo-local = a guard the adopter adopted during genesis reconcile, not in the upstream release. Defaults to upstream when omitted.

skill.description: The skill this gate enforces (its directory name under .claude/skills/). Required in practice for upstream gates; optional because an adopted repo-local guard may enforce no installed skill.

script.description: Repo-relative path to the gate script the consumer repo runs.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 of the trusted gate-script content. Drift from this hash is a parity failure.

test.description: Repo-relative path to the gate's discrimination test (verifiable-quality-gates: every gate ships a test that fails when the gate is neutralized).

lane.description: required = feeds the blocking aggregator; advisory = runs and reports but does not block.

couples.description: File globs that MUST carry this gate: a change touching a matching path must have the gate applied (policy-as-data coupling, as the skill-application receipt uses).

invoke.description: Optional CLI arguments the aggregator passes to the gate script when it runs it (for example, the paths to scan). Each element is passed as a separate argument with no shell, so there is no injection surface. Omit for a gate that needs no arguments (the default). This is how an engineering gate that scans the consumer's code expresses what to scan.
